title: Concentration-Risk Map: Correlated Failures Across Models From One Provider

original_idea.body:
# Concentration-Risk Map: Correlated Failures Across Models From One Provider

**Problem:** A success state requires understanding systemic risk when many systems depend on the same provider/base model. A needed result is empirical evidence on whether models derived from a common base share correlated safety failures.

**Direction:** Take several open models that share a base (e.g. multiple fine-tunes of the same family) and several from unrelated families. Run a fixed jailbreak/safety set and measure whether same-base models fail on the same items more than cross-family models (correlated failure rate). Deliverable: a correlation matrix and an estimate of shared-failure risk.

**Why it matters:** Systemic risk from AI concentration is a named open problem (EU AI Act). If one base model's flaw propagates to all its descendants, a single exploit is systemic. Open models only, inference-only, no lab access - and a genuinely under-explored, counterfactual angle.

**Relevant context:** Context file lists systemic risk from AI concentration (EU AI Act, Intl AI Safety Report 2026) as an open problem; widely-used open base models (Llama/Qwen/Mistral derivatives) make shared-failure testing feasible.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: correlated failures across a shared base mean one exploit is systemic; concrete link to a recognized open problem (EU AI Act).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Run a fixed jailbreak set across models + correlation matrix; standard inference, accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: same-base vs cross-family models, correlated-failure rate, matrix.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, inference-only, no lab access; under-explored systemic-risk angle - neglected gold-type.

novelty.reasoning: Jailbreak transferability studied but a base-lineage correlated-failure map is a plausibly-open angle.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Transferability studied; base-lineage correlation framing plausibly open.
